title: CYBRIK receipt signature statement v1
description: The exact object that is signed when a Tool Fabric control plane signs an execution receipt. The delegated Governor accepted this compact-JWS + RFC-8785-JCS contract profile for implementation only. The statement never carries the receipt itself, only a digest binding: profile + profile_version fix the digest recipe, canonicalization fixes the byte rendering, receipt_contract_id + receipt_contract_version fix which receipt contract those bytes were produced under, and receipt_id + receipt_digest identify the exact receipt. kid names the signer and resolves only against a pinned external trust bundle. Because the profile id is inside the hash input of receipt_digest, a receipt canonicalized under one profile can never be replayed as if it had been signed under another. Status: ACCEPTED FOR IMPLEMENTATION — NOT IMPLEMENTED (v0.2.0; not stable v1/GA). No runtime, signer, key lifecycle, UAT, release, deployment or production authority follows from this file.

profile.description: Receipt digest profile id. The hash input is UTF-8(profile) then one NUL byte then the canonical receipt bytes, so this value is bound into every receipt_digest and cannot be swapped after the fact.

profile_version.description: Version of the profile document, distinct from the profile id itself. 0.2.0 added the required trust_bundle_ref member below, which changes the signed bytes; the receipt digest recipe did not move.

receipt_contract_id.description: $id of the receipt contract the canonical bytes were produced under. Reused unmodified; this F8 packet changes no byte of it.

receipt_contract_version.description: x-cybrik-contract-version of that receipt contract at signing time.

canonicalization.description: Canonical JSON rendering used before hashing: RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme. The exact transmitted receipt is canonicalized with only the top-level receipt_digest and signature removed, and with no schema default materialized — an absent array and an explicitly empty array are two different receipts.

receipt_id.description: receipt_id of the receipt this statement binds. Deliberately no wider and no narrower than the accepted cybrik.execution-receipt.v1 receipt_id: a narrower F8 schema would make receipts the accepted contract permits unsignable under this profile.

receipt_digest.description: Digest produced by the profile above over the exact transmitted receipt.

kid.description: Signer key id. RFC 7638 base64url rendering, without padding, of the SHA-256 over the OKP thumbprint input — the JCS rendering of exactly {crv, kty, x}. A verifier resolves this id ONLY against a pinned external trust bundle, never against key material carried in the message.

signed_at.description: When the control plane signed. Advisory for ordering only; it is not a validity window and confers no freshness guarantee.

trust_bundle_ref.description: The trust-bundle generation the signer bound at signing time, INSIDE the signed bytes. Binding it here rather than only in the transport envelope is what stops an unsigned reference from being swapped for one a verifier already trusts. It is a provenance record, not a precondition: a verifier resolves kid against the bundle it already holds, so a later rotation that retains the signing key does not invalidate this receipt, while a generation that no longer carries the kid fails closed. bundle_uri is a pinned identifier and never a fetch instruction. See OD-F8-7.

bundle_digest.description: SHA-256 over the JCS rendering of the trust bundle document as it stood when this statement was signed.
